title: Sephiria Multiplayer — How to Invite Friends & Open a Co-op Lobby
description: Sephiria multiplayer guide: 4-player online co-op, co-op requirements, creating a Steam lobby, inviting friends, and the host caveats to expect.
meta: For sephiria multiplayer / co-op / invite searches, including a pre-lobby checklist and a troubleshooting table.
body:
Steam lists online co-op for up to four players, with item trading and revives. The session belongs to the host, so a host disconnect is the usual way a run breaks.

Before you open a lobby

The avoidable failures described on this page all happen before the first floor. Settle these five things first.

  1. Both sides finish the prologue and tutorial. An invite cannot skip it, so a guest who has not reached the village has nothing to join.
  2. Decide who hosts by progress. The session is the host’s, so the save that advances is theirs; pick the player furthest along, not the one who asked.
  3. Agree the Artifact and Tablet split. Loot arguments after the first floor are avoidable; the co-op play guide covers the split.
  4. Agree the difficulty while everyone is still in the village. Hard Mode is a per-run choice, so it is settled before the run rather than during it.
  5. Check the Steam Overlay shortcut. Invites arrive through Steam; the overlay defaults to Shift + Tab, and a customised shortcut overrides that default.

How to open a lobby (quick)

  • Finish the prologue and tutorial first — guests have to as well.
  • In the village, find the co-op access point near the dungeon entrance and interact with it.
  • Create a Steam lobby; the creator becomes the host.
  • Invite friends through Steam. There are no in-game lobby codes.

Co-op requirements and party size

ItemValue
ConnectionOnline co-op through Steam
CapacityUp to 4 players total
ProgressHost-authoritative; guests play in the host's session
Shared actionsTrade items, revive fallen teammates
PrologueRequired for the host and for every guest
Community guides describe the access point as a mysterious door or wall in the village; earlier write-ups point at the stone wall by the dungeon entrance. Both agree it is a village interaction that opens after the tutorial.

Host and guest steps

  1. Host: finish the tutorial until the village hub opens.
  2. Host: interact with the co-op access point and choose to create a lobby.
  3. Guest: accept the Steam invite; you join the host's session.
  4. Everyone: agree the Artifact and Tablet split before the first floor — see the co-op play guide.

Host or guest: who does what

StepHostGuest
Before anythingFinish the prologue and tutorialFinish the prologue and tutorial — an invite cannot skip it
Open the lobbyInteract with the Mysterious Door in Bunnyville and choose Create Steam LobbyWait for the lobby to exist; nothing to click yet
InviteSend the Steam invite after the lobby exists, not beforeAccept the newest invitation only
Start the runConfirm the full party is present before descendingSay so immediately if joining stalls, instead of waiting silently

If the host recreates the lobby, old invites stop working — a fresh invite has to go out. Steam Overlay defaults to Shift + Tab, but a customised shortcut wins. Source: community co-op flow recorded on 1.0 (sephiria.net), checked 9 November 2026; the door label varies between write-ups, so follow the in-game prompt.

When it does not work

Each row below maps a symptom to a cause that is already documented on this page. If your symptom is not listed, this page has no answer for it.

SymptomDocumented causeWhat to do
No co-op option anywhereThe access point is a village interaction that opens after the tutorialFinish the prologue and tutorial, then look in the village rather than the title screen
A friend cannot joinEvery guest needs the prologue and tutorial tooHave the guest finish theirs before the next invite
The invite never arrivesInvites go through Steam; there are no in-game lobby codesSend a fresh Steam invite from a live lobby
An old invite does nothingRecreating the lobby invalidates earlier invitesSend a new invite from the recreated lobby
The run ends for everyoneThe session is host-authoritativeRecreate the lobby and re-invite; progress sits with the host

Reviving a downed teammate

  1. Call the down. Name the player and the room so the party stops splitting attention.
  2. Make a pocket. One player pulls or clears nearby threats while another closes the distance.
  3. One reviver. Commit a single player to the prompt and let the rest protect the attempt instead of crowding it.

The 1.0 material confirms revives exist but publishes no revive duration, interruption rule or penalty. Follow the prompt the current build shows rather than a number from an older guide.

Trading without wrecking a build

  • Read the item’s trigger, tag and placement cost before offering it.
  • Name the teammate whose current core can use it now — not the one who might use it later.
  • Drop with the control the inventory shows, then confirm the right item actually left the inventory.
  • Wait until the room is safe before your teammate collects it.

Not every pickup is communal. A trade is worth it when it strengthens a working interaction more than it weakens the giver’s board.

Common mistakes

  • Inviting before the lobby exists. The invite is sent from a live lobby, and a recreated lobby needs a new one.
  • Trusting a screenshot for the door. Write-ups call it a mysterious door, a wall, and the stone wall by the dungeon entrance; follow the prompt your build shows.
  • Descending early. Confirm the full party before the first floor, because a guest still loading cannot be helped from inside a run.
  • Trading away a piece the giver still needs. The trade has to strengthen the party more than it weakens the giver’s board.
  • Assuming shared progress. XP, currency, quest credit and save unlocks are not specified, so check your own save rather than expecting a copy.

What is confirmed, and what is not

QuestionStatusWhat to do
Can players trade items?ConfirmedCoordinate a drop and a pickup
Can players revive teammates?ConfirmedProtect one reviver, follow the prompt
Are XP, currency or quest credit shared?Not specified in 1.0 materialRead the current UI rather than assuming
Do host and guest unlocks save identically?Not specifiedCheck your own save after a session

“Not specified” means the source archive has no statement either way — it is not a guess that the answer is no.

What this page does not cover

This page stops at getting four players into the same run. Role splitting, loot priorities, revive discipline and difficulty for a mixed-skill party are on the co-op play guide. The weapon each player brings is a build question, the six branches are on weapons, the costume trade-offs that decide a first floor are on characters, and the Hard Mode settings are on hard mode.

Quick FAQ

Is there matchmaking with random players?

Nothing in the sources describes random matchmaking. The documented route is a Steam lobby created in the village plus invites sent through Steam, with no in-game lobby codes.

Does a guest keep anything after the session?

Not specified. Whether host and guest unlocks save identically is unrecorded, so check your own save instead of trusting a summary.

Can someone join mid-run?

Not documented. The only join timing described here is before the descent, which is why the host confirms the full party first.

Does the host have to stay for the whole run?

In practice yes. The session belongs to the host and a host disconnect is the usual way a run breaks, so plan around the host’s availability.

Why does the door look different from the guide?

Because the write-ups disagree on the label. All of them place it in the village and behind the tutorial, so follow the in-game prompt rather than a screenshot.
